newsitem.title: UK: Frozen MinFin concerns may boost Russia Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Frozen MinFin concerns may boost Russia Eurobond.

text.p: The launch of Russia's planned debut Eurobond, already dogged by domestic complications, must now contend with turmoil in the Russian MinFin bond market.
But bankers said demand for the Eurobond actually could be boosted by the MinFin fallout. Trading came to a halt amid rumours MinFins totalling more than $50 million had been frozen.
"The Eurobond will be documented under English law and will have Euroclear settlement, which will give some investors comfort," said a syndicate manager familiar with the Eurobond.
"The MinFin situation will remind people of the relative attraction of the liquidity and settlement of an international bond," he said.
Spreads on MinFins, which are dollar-denominated bonds with custody in Russia, have widened by up to 100 basis points during the last week, dealers said.
Dealers said some of the MinFin spread widening could feed through into the Eurobond, expected at the end of November, but it was not the most significant factor.
"It could impact on the Russia pricing to the extent people look at the Eurobond spread as a function of the MinFin spread," said an emerging market debt trader at a U.S. bank.
A dealer at a European bank said: "The MinFin spread widening will not unduly affect the Eurobond. There are more important issues, like whether or not Russia will start negotiations with the IMF."
An International Monetary Fund delegation left Moscow last week without recommending the latest tranche of a three-year loan be released.
The fate of President Boris Yeltsin will also be closely watched, with analysts expecting his heart operation to take place next week.
Roadshows for Russia's debut bond offering start the following week, on November 11, and will be completed in New York on November 20.
"Yeltin's operation, the IMF, MinFins -- there are many considerations for Russia," said the U.S. bank's trader.
"The best that can be hoped for is all information regarding these is known to the market prior to launch," he said.
Russia is expected to issue a five-year bond for up to $500 million. Spread talk has ranged between 350 and 400 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes.
